errors.problem: the tap gloss for the corrected form in the holiday-story 'mistakes' card is wrong on both counts: in كَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ طَوِيلَةً the word means 'long' (a journey), not 'tall', and the -an ending is caused by كَانَتْ ('was'), not by 'is not' (لَيْسَ). The dialogue seg for the same word (lines[3]) correctly says 'long (f, after was)'. The learner tapping the 'right' answer of the mistake card is taught a wrong meaning and a wrong rule.
errors.alsoChange: check the shared tap-gloss dictionary entry for طَوِيلَةً: it seems to have been copied from a لَيْسَ sentence about a tall person

errors.path: scene for cafe: caption (tap gloss of مَقْهَى); content/course/scenarios.json scenarios[3].dialogue.speakers[0].nameAr (tap gloss of مُوَظَّفَة)

errors.current: sāʿa is feminine, so 'possible' takes A / at: mumkina.
errors.problem: engine quirk: a bare ة inside English prose is transliterated as 'A / at' (also 'the number three has no A / at' in pharmacy-visit mistakes[1].why). The Arabic is right; only the generated transliteration line is wrong.

errors.fix: li-Ādam; -ukum (lower-case the clitic, capitalise only the name)

errors.problem: engine quirk: شَاي / الشَّاي is rendered 'shāī' / 'Ash-shāī' (ā + ī) instead of 'shāy'; the final yāʾ with no vowel is a consonant here. Also 'Tafaḍḍali sh-shāī' in family-visit lines[8]. The Arabic is right.

errors.path: scene for appointment-time: caption; scene for appointment-time spots[12].ar
errors.problem: engine quirk: words whose al- alif carries a kasra (الِانْتِظَار, الِاسْتِقْبَال) are transliterated 'liāntiẓār' and 'Iliāstiqbāl' instead of 'l-intiẓār' / 'al-istiqbāl'. The Arabic is right.

notes.note: 'The tea is really very delicious' doubles the intensifier; الشَّاي لَذِيذ جِدًّا is simply 'The tea is very delicious'.
'The road is very crowded today' adds 'very'; the Arabic الطَّرِيق مُزْدَحِم الْيَوْم has no جِدًّا. Harmless, but the segs do not support 'very'.

هَلْ أَذْهَبُ يَمِينًا هُنَا أَوْ يَسَارًا؟ is acceptable everyday MSA, but in a formal alternative question أَمْ is preferred (the directions scenario uses ثُمَّ يَمِينًا أَمْ يَسَارًا correctly). Consider aligning the two scenarios.

مَبْرُوك! is rendered 'Enjoy it!'; the seg correctly says 'congratulations'. The cultural equivalent is fine, but a beginner may not connect the two; 'Congratulations (on your new dress)!' would match the seg.

الْمِنْضَدَة is glossed 'the counter'; its usual meaning is a (small) table. If the photo shows a serving counter, الطَّاوِلَة/الْمِنْضَدَة are both defensible, but مِنْضَدَة = 'table' is the dictionary sense a learner will meet elsewhere.

The dialogue is about Luxor and Aswan (Egypt) but the photo scene is Al-Khazneh in Petra, Jordan. Not an error, but the mismatch may puzzle learners; a Luxor temple or Nile balloon photo would match the story.

الدَّرَّاجَةُ النَّارِيَّة (motorbike) is correct; the tap gloss for the first word alone says 'the bicycle', which is right for دَرَّاجَة by itself and the second gloss explains the compound. Fine as is, just flagging that the learner has to read both glosses.

In the intro transliterations the first phrase after 'Useful phrases:' is capitalised (e.g. 'Min faḍlika (please), urīdu (I want)'), which looks like inconsistent casing; cosmetic engine behaviour, not a content error.

summary: I read all 16 scenarios in audit/scenarios-1.txt (cafe, taxi, morning-routine, appointment-time, restaurant, bakery, directions, clothes-shop, renting-flat, family-visit, lost-luggage, holiday-story, doctor, pharmacy-visit, birthday-invitation, weather-plans) in full: every intro, speaker name, culture note, dialogue line with its English and segs, every mistakes right/wrong pair and its 'why', every quiz answer key and option, and every photo-scene caption, spot label, note and tap gloss. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: harakat, case endings (accusative after كَانَ/لَيْسَ, -an objects, يَوْمَ, مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ), number–noun agreement (ثَلَاثَ كَعْكَات, خَمْسَةُ أَرْغِفَة, عَشْرُ دَقَائِق, سِتّ سَنَوَات, بِعَشَرَة جُنَيْهَات vs خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ جُنَيْهًا), moods after لَمْ/لَنْ/أَنْ, feminine and dual imperatives, the kasra on كَمِ/هَلِ/تَفَضَّلِ before al- and the non-human plural → feminine singular rule are all correct, and all quiz answer keys and mistakes pairs check out (the bakery arithmetic 10+30+30=70, change 30 is also right). I found 11 errors: 1 major and 10 minor. The one major finding is a wrong tap gloss on the corrected form in the holiday-story mistakes card (طَوِيلَةً glossed 'tall (f, after is not)' instead of 'long (f, after was)'). The pattern behind the minor findings is the shared tap-gloss dictionary: scene spot glosses that pick another sense of the word than the one in the photo or sentence (رَصِيف 'platform' for a pavement, عَمُود 'pole' for a pillar/column, سَاعَة 'hour' for a wall clock, إِشَارَة 'pointing' for a traffic light, حَارّ 'hot (weather)' for a chili), plus spurious '(of)' on مَقْهَى and مُوَظَّفَة. The four engine quirks named in the brief (bare ة → 'A / at', capitalised name after a clitic, شَاي → 'shāī', kasra-alif words → 'liāntiẓār'/'Iliāstiqbāl') each occur and are reported once. 8 notes cover English wording, one أَوْ/أَمْ register point, the Petra photo for a Luxor story and a 'counter' gloss.
